newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SHELL SEES KUDU RESERVE ESTIMATE IN 2 WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SEES KUDU RESERVE ESTIMATE IN 2 WEEKS.

text.p: Initial indications of the size of the reserves of Namibia's Kudu gas field should be available in two weeks' time, Shell Exploration and Production Namibia managing director Ger Kegge said on Wednesday.

Commenting on speculation in some international newsletters that Kudu could have reserves of between seven trillion cubic feet (tcf) and 14 tcf, making it a world class gas deposit, Kegge said it was too early to tell.

"The Kudu gas accumulation has the potential to be large, but it is too early to say... We expect that we will start flaring Sunday night or Monday and the results should be ready the week thereafter," he said.
However, the full implication of those results will only be known in a few months.

"One of the objectives of the well that we are drilling is to prove gas towards a three tcf reserve base and basically we will have to find out after we have done our work how far we have come," he said.
Shell started drilling the Kudu-4 well in August. In partnership with Energy Africa, it was awarded the exploration licence over Kudu in May 1993 and Texaco joined the venture this year.

Kegge welcomed the announcement on Wednesday by South African Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna that he was preparing a gas policy to help promote the use of gas from Kudu and Mozambique's Pande gas field.

"I am very happy about that because it would only help us to market the gas because for economies of scale the volumes of gas that we have to produce may be too much for Namibia on its own," Kegge said.
